To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that

the number of countries using good to very good quality remote sensing (RS)- and national forest inventory (NFIs)-based data sources for reporting on forest resources increased from 55 and 48 in 2005 to a global coverage of ∼85% in 2020.

the use of remote-sensing and national forest inventory data for national reporting on forests to the Food and Agricultural Organization of the United Nations (FAO) has improved in the last 15 years and that this is more pronounced in tropical countries.
globally, 99 countries monitor forest area using good to very good RS capacities, while 102 countries have good to very good national forest inventory capacities.
In summary, our research is concerned with

the question of whether and to what extent the global monitoring of forests has improved in recent years, which has important implications for the monitoring of the global forest carbon sink and other global forest functions and services.

the following: (a) the use of RS and NFI for monitoring forest resources, (b) the data quality used for national reporting to FAO FRA, and (c), in particular, changes in national forest reporting capacities in tropical countries.
the following questions: What are the data sources used for national reporting on forests?
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
the quality of national forest monitoring data sources is generally improving, but that there are still significant challenges to overcome in many countries.
the quality of data sources used for national reporting to FRA 2020 is good to very good for most countries, with a few exceptions.
national forest monitoring capacities are increasing, and that this is reflected by the quality of the data reported to FAO.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
the global forest monitoring capacities have improved over the last 15 years, especially in the tropics.
the global data basis for reporting forest information is improving.
national reporting to the FAO FRA 2005-2020 is based on a solid data basis, and that the capacity to monitor and report on forest resources has improved in the past 15 years.
The main takeaway from our work is that
the global forest area is increasingly monitored at good to very high capacities, and that there are strong linkages between improved governance and national capacities for forest monitoring.

countries with persistent good to very high monitoring capacities for forest area and growing stock in FRA 2000–2020 have been the most successful in reporting high-quality data on forest area, growing stocks, and carbon stocks in FRA 202020.
countries are increasingly using RS and/or NFI to monitor forest area, growing stocks, and carbon stock, and the data quality has improved over the past 15 years, especially in the tropics.
